record.original_question: Can motivic integration, or a suitable stringy invariant, be used to prove a Grothendieck-Ogg-Shafarevich type formula in the wild setting?

evidence.quote: Problem 11.2. Can we show a Grothendieck-Ogg-Shafarevich type formula by using motivic integration and/or a version of stringy invariant?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p > 0, and let F be a constructible ℓ-adic sheaf on X (with ℓ ≠ p) which is wildly ramified at a finite set S ⊂ X of closed points. The classical Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula expresses the Euler–Poincaré characteristic χ(X∖S, F) in terms of the generic rank of F and the local Swan conductors Sw_x(F) at the points of wild ramification:

   χ_c(X∖S, F) = rk(F) · χ(X∖S) − Σ_{x∈S} Sw_x(F).

Motivic integration, in the sense of Kontsevich, Denef–Loeser, Sebag, and its variants for formal schemes and Deligne–Mumford stacks, assigns to a variety with mild singularities (or to an arc/jet space) an invariant in a Grothendieck ring of varieties; "stringy invariants" (Batyrev) provide a related class of motivic invariants of singular varieties that incorporate discrepancy data.

Problem. Develop a proof of a Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich-type formula in the wild ramification setting (for ℓ-adic sheaves on varieties over a field of positive characteristic, or more generally for sheaves on schemes over a complete discrete valuation ring with wild ramification along a divisor) using motivic integration and/or a suitable stringy invariant. Concretely: produce a motivic-integration formula whose specialization recovers the Swan-conductor terms appearing in a Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich-type identity for the Euler characteristic, and use this to give a new proof of such a formula in wildly ramified situations where existing proofs (via Kato–Saito ramification theory, etc.) apply, or in situations where no such proof is currently known.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction. While there is substantial work connecting motivic integration to wild ramification (e.g. Yasuda's program on the wild McKay correspondence, and Kato–Saito's higher-dimensional ramification theory), no published result appears to provide a motivic-integration / stringy-invariant proof of a Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich-type formula in the wild setting. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Motivic integration, the McKay correspondence and wild ramification (Yasuda)
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph developing motivic integration over wildly ramified Galois covers and the wild McKay correspondence; does not establish a GOS-type formula via these methods.
status_evidence.claim: Motivic integration has been developed in the wild setting (wild McKay correspondence) but a GOS-type formula via these tools is not established.

status_evidence.title: Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Classical formula for Euler characteristic of ℓ-adic sheaves on curves involving Swan conductor; higher-dimensional generalizations due to Kato–Saito (2008).
status_evidence.claim: Standard proofs of GOS use ramification theory, not motivic integration; motivic-integration proof remains a separate question.
